cells.tense: You are at the edge of what you gathered, and you are moving on with it.
cells.ask: Leave one thing gathered where it is and walk toward what it points to next.
cells.core:
You know what's behind you and what you're walking toward. The leaving is real and you're not pretending it's nothing — you gathered it, you carried it, and now you can set it down without dropping it. The choice is settled enough that you don't keep explaining it.

What holds it together is that you're not spending the walk looking back. Your mind is settled on the direction, so the small corrections happen inside the movement instead of replacing it. One calm keeps the crossing possible, and it's the same calm that lets you hold the harder parts without rushing.

Keep the direction visible somewhere, and let it stay a little unfinished.
cells.sheetLine: You know what you're walking toward, and the walking holds.
cells.verb: walking from a gathered meaning toward the one that connects deeper
cells.place: a chosen direction, at the point where the leaving gets decided

cells.tense: You are walking past rooms you'll never enter, guarding a door you already crossed.
cells.ask: Let one version stand in view for a day and don't rework it into a verdict.
cells.core:
You keep running ahead of the step you're in — a choice turns into a test, a gathering into a verdict you might fail. The direction you already set gets re-audited in your head, and the energy that should go into what you make goes into guarding a gate nobody's actually at.

What's moving forward is real. The doubling back is what's costing you. Coming back to one thing that's already happening — one draft out where someone can see it, one plan you don't revise tonight — is the repair. The work is the work, at the scale it's actually asking for now, and the rest is rehearsal.

Pushing harder on the crossing is what's fraying it.

cells.tense: You are addressing a house you no longer live in, drafting a letter that won't send.
cells.ask: Trace two rooms you've been between and say the one thing they share.
cells.core:
The walk is behind you and the voice hasn't come with it — holding the leaving ready to explain, so the explanation is the only thing with somewhere to point. When the answer is the leaving, the direction hasn't gotten a place to stand.

Stepping back far enough to see the whole shape is what's called for — the room you're in, the one you came from, and what the two of them have in common. When the pattern finds a place to live, the direction gets something to point at. Saying the shape out loud, or writing it into what you're already describing, does that job at this scale. Observing is doing it here.

cells.tense: The leaving is already being written, and you keep filing it as weather.
cells.ask: Name two options you're between, out loud, to one person, without picking yet.
cells.core:
A direction is already moving — shorter answers, dropped routines, the asking that stopped. You'd call it the season, or things being busy. But a choice is running that nobody has claimed as a choice, and because it's unnamed, the smaller moves keep getting read as distance instead of direction.

Saying it isn't a verdict. It's admitting one of those smaller moves is yours, once, to somebody who isn't keeping score. Then your direction has something to stand on, and the drift stops being the thing you measure.

One plain sentence about what's already shifting costs less than another month of calling it the season.
cells.sheetLine: You're already moving on. Calling it the season gets heavy.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: that Passage leaves people (transmission getting past them) — the record says the card is inner/expansive at the outer face, so a reader could say they're building something, not leaving. The cross-twin line (fortitude/steadiness for Too Much, logic/pattern for Too Little) is named on the map and stays put; no history, no cost, no who, no motive. The asks survive a wrong read because each one is doable without my diagnosis: leaving one file and the ending uncorrected, letting one structure stand a day, saying the shape and leaving it uncorrected, and laying out one or two options with the deciding for later. The sentence that serves me more than the person: 'the rebuilding runs behind everything they do' — that's a claim about their history I have not been given, so it goes.
